prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us ranked B001 first, which I do not treat as merit in itself, so I re-examined it on the substance. It is a specific discovery with a discernible change in the field: proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic, glucagonostatic and satiety actions, and the receptor pathway. These are well documented, replicated in humans, and have been followed by decades of independent clinical confirmation and large outcome trials. The impact is neither speculative nor premature. The three-person basic-science trio of Holst (human physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor mechanisms) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) is the cleanest attribution available under the cap, and it fits a physiology-or-medicine prize because it recognises discovery rather than only drug design.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution, not importance. Priority for identifying the active GLP-1 form is contested, and Habener, who is not in the supplied credit, belongs in that discussion. Excluding Knudsen means the prize honours the physiology and not the long-acting analogues that actually changed treatment, so one can argue the citation covers only half of the story the public will associate with it. A three-person cap forces an allocation that someone will see as unfair, and I have not independently verified the priority history, which rests on my general knowledge.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranked TNF blockade (B010) second, as fully mature, clean in attribution with Feldmann and Maini, and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree on the cleanliness of the Feldmann-Maini pairing and on maturity, and it is the better-attributed case. But my own test is whether the field changed because of a specific discovery, and I read B010 as a strong translational and clinical-trial achievement built on an existing cytokine framework, whereas B001 spans original physiology through to therapy. I would keep B010 as a serious later candidate rather than place it above the top three. I also take her point that age may argue for acting sooner, but that is a timing consideration and not a reason to rank it higher on merit.

responses.point: Sandberg ranked the unfolded protein response (B051, Mori and Walter) second and called it a clean two-person pair of conceptual originality, while noting that clinical translation is limited and that the PERK/eIF2 arm is not credited.
responses.response: I put B051 third and respect the conceptual originality, but I disagree that the omission of the eIF2alpha/PERK arm is a minor simplification. A pair of Walter and Mori would define the prize around IRE1 and HAC1/XBP1 and leave the integrated stress response branch out, so the citation could be criticised as incomplete. Combined with limited clinical translation, I would not rank it above CAR-T or optogenetics this year, though it is a legitimate basic-science candidate for a later one.

responses.point: El Manira put optogenetics (B012) second as a methodological advance with very high originality, and accepted that any trio of the six credited names excludes deserving people.
responses.response: I largely share his scientific assessment, since I ranked B012 second, but the attribution problem makes me more cautious than he is. Nagel and Hegemann with Deisseroth is defensible, yet Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have substantive claims, and I do not think we should crown a method while knowingly leaving out half the discovery chain. The tool-versus-discovery question also remains open. This is why I support B001 as the 2026 configuration and keep B012 as an alternative.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranked CAR-T (B017) second and treated the missing foundational credit for the chimeric receptor concept as an open question that does not undermine the core discovery.
responses.response: I accept that the clinical evidence is strong, but I place more weight on the attribution gap than he does. Eshhar and other early receptor designers are outside the supplied credit, and with Rosenberg's contribution best described as adoptive cell transfer, a June, Sadelain and Rosenberg trio does not map onto a single clean discovery. Because the field is still evolving in solid tumours and long-term safety, I would keep B017 as my first alternative rather than the preferred configuration.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, ranked B001 first but placed BCR-ABL inhibition (B004) third, citing exceptional patient impact and a mature, replicated paradigm of targeted therapy.
responses.response: I agree B004 is clinically exceptional and mature, but I am less persuaded that it is primarily a discovery prize. The credited names are mostly drug-development and clinical figures, while the foundational BCR-ABL work of Rowley, Baltimore and others lies outside the credit. This is the same concern as with Knudsen in B001, but it is stronger here, so I would rank B004 below the two or three cases where the credited names cover the discovery itself.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to the active GLP-1 peptide, relative to Habener's group, is settled well enough for her to be named without reservation.
Whether the committee should favour the physiology trio or substitute Knudsen for one of them to recognise the drug-development arm.
Whether a 2026 prize on B001 should be paired with a second distinct achievement; the three-person cap makes that difficult.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My documented co-authorship with Per Svenningsson and Abdel El Manira concerns other work and does not involve any candidate, and I do not infer ties from shared institutions or from my own field of nuclear receptors and dopamine-neuron development.
